Purpose: Code repository, version control, collaboration, and project management. Essential for managing research code and collaborating with team members.
Notes:
Apply for GitHub Education Pack (free with university email) — includes free Copilot, team plans.
Use .gitignore for large data files.
GitHub Actions for CI/CD pipeline testing.

Purpose: Storing datasets, notes, backup files, and sharing large files. Cloud storage for research materials.
Notes:
Good for: backing up raw datasets, sharing large files, storing survey exports.
Create shared research folder.
University Google account may have unlimited storage.
Use backup & sync for automatic backups.

Purpose: Running heavy data processing code in cloud using free GPU/TPU. Ideal for machine learning model training, large-scale data processing, and computationally intensive analysis.
Notes:
Free tier: T4 GPU (16GB), ~12GB RAM, 12-hour sessions.
Sufficient for many ML training tasks.
Save notebooks to Google Drive.
Colab Pro ($10/mo) is worth it for larger training jobs — priority GPU + longer runtimes.

Purpose: Setting up search alerts, saving paper libraries, tracking citations, and exporting references. Account features complement the search platform.
Notes:
Already covered as platform in Research Platforms sheet.
Account features: email alerts for keywords, saved paper libraries, citation tracking.
Use personal Gmail for persistent alerts across devices.

Purpose: Collaborative LaTeX document writing and editing. Write research papers, reports, or theses with real-time collaboration.
Notes:
Free tier: 1 project limit, 120s compile.
Check if your university has an institutional Overleaf license (many universities do).
Link with GitHub for version control.
Use master.tex + chapter subfiles structure for larger documents.

Purpose: Creating and distributing surveys for primary data collection. Useful for perception studies, market research, and gathering responses from target populations.
Notes:
Free, unlimited responses, CSV export.
Use section breaks for multi-page surveys.
Test with pilot respondents first.
Response validation for quality control.
Good for: questionnaires, feedback forms, registration forms.

Purpose: Managing paper citations, organizing PDFs, generating bibliographies. Open-source with excellent LaTeX integration via Better BibTeX.
Notes:
Zotero recommended over Mendeley: (1) Browser connector saves papers one-click, (2) Better BibTeX extension for LaTeX .bib export, (3) Group libraries for team collaboration.
Organize papers into thematic folders matching your research topics.

Purpose: Primary code editor for development, data analysis scripts, LaTeX writing, and dashboard development. Extensible with thousands of extensions.
Notes:
Essential extensions: Python (Microsoft), LaTeX Workshop (James Yu), GitLens (GitKraken), Live Share (real-time collaboration), GitHub Copilot (AI assistance), YAML, Rainbow CSV, Docker.
Settings sync via GitHub account.

Purpose: Python environment management for data science and machine learning projects. Conda environments for managing project dependencies across different tools and frameworks.
Notes:
Create separate conda environments for different project components to manage dependencies cleanly.
Use environment.yml files for reproducibility.
Miniconda (lightweight) recommended over full Anaconda — install only what you need.

Purpose: Containerization platform for reproducible development environments. Package applications and data processing pipelines into portable containers.
Notes:
Write Dockerfiles for individual services and docker-compose.yml for full stack orchestration.
Ensures reproducibility across different machines.
Docker Hub for sharing container images.
Free for personal use.

Purpose: Local LaTeX distribution for compiling documents offline on Windows. Alternative: TeX Live (cross-platform).
Notes:
Easiest LaTeX distribution on Windows.
Install Perl (for latexmk) and use VS Code LaTeX Workshop extension for integrated compile.
Auto-installs missing packages on-the-fly.
Also use: latexmk -xelatex for compilation.

Purpose: Create figures and diagrams: architecture diagrams, workflow charts, methodology figures, pipeline visualizations.
Notes:
VS Code extension available (draw.io integration).
Templates for: flowcharts, network diagrams, architecture diagrams.
Export to: SVG (vector — best for publications), PNG, PDF.
Use for: pipeline architecture, methodology flow, comparison visualizations.

Purpose: Writing assistance for academic papers, reports, and other documents. Grammar, clarity, tone, and vocabulary improvements.
Notes:
Grammarly Premium has .edu discount.
Free tier catches: spelling, grammar, punctuation.
Premium: clarity improvements, tone detection, plagiarism check.
LanguageTool is an open-source alternative.
Use for final polish of documents before submission.

Purpose: Plagiarism detection and similarity checking. Required by many institutions before final submission of dissertations or theses.
Notes:
Check if your institution provides Turnitin access.
Most universities do.
Submit document chapters before final submission to check similarity score.
Target: <20% similarity.
Exclude bibliography and quoted material.
Alternative: Grammarly Premium includes plagiarism checking.

Purpose: Project management for research teams. Track progress, assign tasks, manage timeline and milestones.
Notes:
Notion recommended for project tracking.
Create: shared workspace with pages for each deliverable, task board for team members, timeline view for deadlines, meeting notes database.
Free for personal use with unlimited pages.
Trello is a simpler alternative if Notion is too much.

Purpose: Team communication for daily coordination among research team members and supervisors.
Notes:
Slack recommended for channel-based organization (#literature-review, #data-collection, #writing), file sharing, integration with GitHub/Google Drive.
Free Slack: 90-day message history, 10 app integrations.
WhatsApp is a simpler alternative widely used for instant communication.

Purpose: Large file storage extension for Git. Store datasets, model files, and other large assets without bloating the repository.
Cost: Free tier (1 GB storage, 1 GB bandwidth/month) + Paid
Notes:
CSV datasets and model files are often too large for regular Git (GitHub has 100MB file limit).
Git LFS handles them.
Install: git lfs install.
Track: git lfs track '*.csv' '*.pth' '*.h5'.
Free tier: 1 GB storage — enough for CSV datasets but not large model checkpoints.

Purpose: FTP/SFTP client for deploying web applications to shared hosting servers.
Notes:
Connect via SFTP (SSH) for security.
Transfer: compiled assets, vendor folder, uploads.
Use .gitignore to exclude sensitive files.
WinSCP is a Windows alternative with sync features.

Purpose: Data visualization platform for creating interactive charts and dashboards for research figures.
Notes:
Create interactive visualizations of research findings.
Free Tableau Public: publish to web, unlimited visualizations.
Good for: comparison charts, trend lines, cross-group comparisons.
Embed screenshots in documents or supplement with interactive web versions.

Purpose: Zotero extension that automatically generates .bib files for LaTeX. Keeps citations synchronized between Zotero and Overleaf or local LaTeX editors.
Notes:
Install in Zotero → exports .bib file automatically on any change.
Features: (1) citation keys like author2024title, (2) auto-export to .bib file, (3) drag-and-drop citations from Zotero to LaTeX, (4) works with Overleaf via WebDAV sync or manual upload.
